Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

mixvlmc 0.3.0

This release introduces a class for discrete time series, a new representation of context trees with a LaTeX output integrated with knitr, and fixes numerous bugs. Several changes break compatibility with previous versions, in particular some bug fixes change the models obtained with VLMC with covariates (see the breaking changes below).

Breaking changes

Model representation (with draw())

  • draw() returns a representation of the context tree (an object of class mixvlmc_draw) instead of the context tree itself. The representation is printed automatically, so that draw(model) displays the tree as before in the console, but not any more when the result is not printed, for instance inside a function or a loop (use print(draw(model)))
  • draw() has now a second parameter format ("text" when it is missing, see below). Passing the control list as the second argument of draw() is deprecated (it is still supported with a warning)
  • the digits parameter of draw.covlmc() is deprecated and replaced by a similar parameter in draw_control()
  • draw() methods report an error when they are given unused arguments, for instance an option of draw_control() given directly to draw() (they were silently ignored)
  • defaults for draw.covlmc() have changed (issue #66):
    • p_value is now FALSE by default
    • when p_value is TRUE the p-values are represented between separators given by the open_p_value and close_p_value members of the control list. Defaults are < and >
    • the intercept is separated from other coefficients by the characters specified in the intercept_sep member of the control list. Defaults to " & "
    • the characters used to separate levels from models are now " ~ "
    • temporal blocks are now separated by default by the time_sep member of the control list. The default value is set to " | " and the time_sep parameter of draw.covlmc() is deprecated
    • the new parameter constant_as_prob is TRUE by default, which also modifies the default display
  • the interface of draw_control() has been significantly changed (issue #66) which should break most customisation code at the level of characters used by draw() to display a model
  • with the ASCII charset (charset_ascii()), the intermediate children of a node are introduced by +-- like the first one (they were introduced by '-- like the last one)
  • in the LaTeX format of draw.covlmc(), logical covariates are named with their level (day[TRUE]), consistently with factors and with the text format
  • the counts of draw.ctx_tree() (with frequency = "detailed") are separated by ", " as in draw.vlmc() (they were separated by ",")

Estimation and use of models

  • the C++ backend is the default backend of ctx_tree(), vlmc() and tune_vlmc() (option mixvlmc.backend) and is not considered experimental any more. It gives the same models as the R backend, which remains available with backend = "R" or options(mixvlmc.backend = "R"), e.g. to process context trees in R. covlmc() is not concerned
  • the package now depends on R >= 4.1.0 (this was already implied by its dependencies)
  • the degrees of freedom of the likelihood ratio tests used by covlmc() and prune.covlmc() take into account the number of levels of factor covariates (a factor with L levels has L-1 parameters per time step, not 1). This changes the models obtained with factors with at least 3 levels
  • unused levels of factor covariates are ignored by covlmc() (they used to change the fitted model)
  • the multinom engine of covlmc() detects rank deficient models (e.g.  collinear covariates) consistently with the glm engine
  • the number of parameters of a covlmc (used by AIC and BIC, in particular in tune_covlmc()) does not depend on the computing engine any more (the multinom engine, and the glm engine with two states, counted the unused levels of factor covariates, while the glm engine with three states or more ignored the states absent from the data of a context). Each context counts one intercept per state but one, as for VLMC, and the coefficients of the covariates actually estimated by the logistic model, which ignores the states that do not follow the context and the unused levels of factors (see loglikelihood.covlmc()). The likelihood ratio tests still use the nominal number of parameters
  • the models associated with the root of the context tree of a covlmc (depth 0 models, extended model used for the first observation) use all the observations (the first one was ignored)
  • loglikelihood() returns -Inf on new data containing a transition that has a zero probability according to the model (the R backend of vlmc() ignored such transitions)
  • print() and summary() of tune_vlmc() and tune_covlmc() results report the log likelihood used for model selection
  • with the C++ backend, tune_vlmc() increases max_depth as documented (and as with the R backend) and max_depth = 0 means a depth 0 model (it meant no limit)
  • with the C++ backend, simulate() with sample = "fast" (the default) gives results that do not depend on the platform any more: for a given seed, they differ from the ones of previous versions
  • metrics() reports an error when it is applied to a node of a VLMC that is not a context (it returned NaN values), as it does for VLMC with covariates
  • methods that do not use their ... argument now report an error when additional arguments are given (issue #64). Misspelled arguments such as simulate(model, 100, burn_in = 10) or loglikelihood(model, new_data = x) were silently ignored. This applies also to the type argument of contexts(), which was removed in mixvlmc 0.2.0 and ignored since then

New features

Discrete time series class (dts)

In order to ease the introduction of multiple time series support, a single discrete time series can now be represented by the dts class, via the dts() function (see issue #76). All functions that use discrete time series now accept objects of this class in addition to simple vectors of a supported type (numeric, factor, character and logical). This applies to model estimation functions such as vlmc() or covlmc(), to model selection functions (e.g. tune_vlmc()) but also to functions that use new data such as loglikelihood() and predict.vlmc().

Model representation (with draw())

A major change of draw() is the support of multiple output formats. This is done via a format parameter. It currently supports:

  • the format of previous versions of mixvlmc with format="text". This is the default text based representation.
  • a new LaTeX export with format="latex" based on the LaTeX package forest (https://ctan.org/pkg/forest) as per issue #66. This can be used to include (CO)VLMC models in LaTeX documents, for instance when using rmarkdown or quarto.

In addition, the text based model representation has been improved (as per issue #66) as follows:

  • a new global option mixvlmc.charset can be used to select the characters used by draw() when format="text" between pure ASCII and UTF-8
  • when possible, the text based representation defaults to UTF-8 symbols to provide a cleaner display of the context tree
  • full customisation of the character set has moved from draw_control() to charset_ascii() and charset_utf8()
  • the draw.covlmc() function uses arguably better default parameters (described above)
  • when a logistic model does not use the covariates, it is now represented by draw.covlmc() as a VLMC node, that is with the probability distribution on the state space that it represents

The result of draw() integrates with knitr (issue #77): in an R Markdown or Quarto document that produces LaTeX (e.g. a PDF document), draw(model, "latex") renders the tree and adds the forest package to the preamble of the document. format() and as.character() give the representation as a character vector.

Minor improvements

  • summary() of a VLMC is much faster with the R backend (about 13 times on a model with 9,000 contexts)
  • the computations of the C++ backend (construction of the context trees and simulation) can be interrupted
  • tune_covlmc() has a control parameter to specify the control parameters of the models (see covlmc_control()), e.g. pseudo_obs
  • the progress of tune_vlmc() and tune_covlmc() (with verbose > 0) is reported with message() (instead of being printed), so that it can be silenced with suppressMessages()
  • vlmc(), cutoff() and prune() are faster with the R backend (about 40% for vlmc())
  • covlmc() and tune_covlmc() are faster (about 15%) and the models they return use much less memory (about a third), as the ROC curves of the logistic models are not computed and stored any more (their AUC is computed directly)
  • cutoff() applied to a node of a VLMC with covariates returns the p-values of the likelihood ratio tests associated with the node (it returned a meaningless VLMC cut off)
  • metrics() supports trimmed VLMC with covariates (it reported an error): the accuracy and the confusion matrix are computed from the ones of the contexts, while the AUC is NA (with a warning)
  • a covlmc records the computing engine used to estimate it (option mixvlmc.predictive) and prune.covlmc() uses it to estimate new logistic models, with a warning if the option has been changed in between (the current engine was used, possibly mixing engines in a model)
  • print() and summary() describe a covlmc as a “VLMC with covariates” (instead of “VLMC with covariate”)

Bug fixes

Input validation

  • prune.covlmc() checks that alpha is in (0, 1] and warns when it is larger than the alpha of the model
  • covlmc_control() and covlmc() check that pseudo_obs is a positive number, and covlmc() rejects a covariate data frame without columns
  • missing values and empty time series are rejected (they crashed R with the R backend), as well as missing values in covariates
  • states that do not appear in the time series (e.g. unused levels of a factor) are supported
  • min_size, max_depth and the ignore parameter of loglikelihood() are validated (min_size = 0 led to an exponential computation time)
  • time series with a single state (e.g. a constant series or a factor with a single level) are rejected by the estimation functions (they led to a degenerate model with the R backend and to an error with the C++ backend)

VLMC

  • the AUC of a context of a VLMC (metrics() of a node and contexts(metrics = TRUE)) is NA: as the predictions of a context are constant, it was always 0.5 or NA
  • the time series produced by simulate() (for VLMC and VLMC with covariates) do not print their class as an attribute any more
  • children() and merged_with() report the states of models fitted on a factor (they reported their integer codes when the sequence of the node had been given as a character vector, e.g. to find_sequence())
  • tune_vlmc() and tune_covlmc() increase a null max_depth instead of warning that they cannot find a suitable value
  • contexts() with local = TRUE reports correct positions and supports metrics = TRUE (R backend)
  • positions of the empty context are 0 based in all cases and are not reported any more after trim()
  • simulate() discards the correct number of values during the burn in period for depth 0 models (R backend)
  • loglikelihood() with ignore and without newdata works with the C++ backend
  • contexts(frequency = "detailed") names the frequencies by the states for factors with the C++ backend
  • the documentation of loglikelihood() states correctly that the default likelihood function is the truncated one

VLMC with covariates

  • the cut off values given by cutoff.covlmc() (with raw = FALSE) are smaller than the p-values by a relative margin, so that pruning with them has an effect even when the p-values recomputed by prune.covlmc() differ in the last digits from the ones stored in the model, as with some linear algebra libraries (e.g. MKL). tune_covlmc() could report models identical to the previous one and return different results for different values of max_depth
  • children() of a node of a VLMC with covariates returns nodes of VLMC with covariates (they were nodes of context trees, without the logistic models and the merged contexts)
  • the coefficients of constant models (contexts followed by a single state) with three states or more are expressed with respect to the first state, as for the other models: they were expressed with respect to the last state, so that draw() (with constant_as_prob = FALSE) and contexts() (with model = "coef") reported them under the wrong states
  • the logistic models of a covlmc do not keep references to the functions that fitted them: saved models (e.g. with saveRDS()) were several times larger than the models themselves, up to 20 times for the models returned by tune_covlmc()
  • the logistic models without covariates (intercept only) obey the mixvlmc.maxit option with the glm and multinom engines
  • the mixvlmc.maxit option is used by VGAM::vglm() (three states or more with the glm engine): VGAM replaced it by its own default (31 iterations), and models stopped at this limit could be reported as not converged
  • the likelihood of degenerate multinom models is not NA any more (which crashed covlmc()) and NaN likelihoods with zero probabilities are avoided, including in ignored observations
  • metrics() works with constant models and at least 3 states, and per context metrics of degenerate vglm and multinom models are correct
  • metrics() and predict() work on depth 0 models
  • multinom models with many parameters are supported (MaxNWts)
  • cutoff() ignores correctly intercept only leaves with at least 3 states
  • find_sequence() handles correctly merged contexts
  • metrics() on a node which is not a context gives a clear error

C++ backend

  • out of bounds accesses (which led to fake contexts in ctx_tree() with min_size = 1 and to crashes in draw()) and memory leaks are fixed
  • long repeats in the time series do not overflow the stack any more
  • pruned models are restored correctly after serialisation (e.g. after saveRDS()/readRDS()), as well as positions and models obtained with as_vlmc() from a context tree. Notice that pruned models saved with previous versions are still restored incorrectly
  • is_context() and local counts are correct for all nodes of a context tree
  • the depth of a context tree does not include the end of the time series
  • context trees of time series shorter than min_size are reduced to their root (they caused an error), and cutoff() works on such models
  • trim() removes positions from context trees
  • simulate() uses base::sample.int() even if another function with the same name is defined in the global environment

Documentation

  • the bootstrap example of vignette("sampling") used no burn in period, as the burnin argument of simulate() was misspelled
  • the vignettes and the README have been proofread: in particular, the text of vignette("prediction") and vignette("sampling") now agrees with the models they select, and vignette("variable-length-markov-chains") gives the correct number of parameters of a Markov chain of order m

mixvlmc 0.2.2

CRAN release: 2025-05-26

This is a bug fix release (see issue #79 for the main bugs):

  • fix a bug in the C++ suffix tree implementation (subscript out of bounds in rare cases)
  • avoid NaN production in loglikelihood() and related functions for the multinom predictive engine
  • handle situations when a merged or local model has more degrees of freedom that the models it is supposed to replace (in covlmc)
  • improve the interaction with the VGAM package in corner cases with degenerate models

mixvlmc 0.2.1

CRAN release: 2023-10-31

This release has no visible changes and fixes internal issues:

  • missing package in Suggests
  • double definition of a C++ internal function

mixvlmc 0.2.0

CRAN release: 2023-10-28

Breaking changes

  • the mode parameter of cutoff.vlmc() has been renamed to scale
  • the type parameter has been removed from contexts() variants and the default result format has been modified significantly
  • the counts parameter from contexts.vlmc() and contexts.covlmc() has been replaced by a logical parameter named local
  • contexts() sequences are now reported by default in temporal order

New features

C++ backend

The main major new feature of this version is the inclusion of a C++ implementation of context tree and VLMC construction. A new option mixvlmc.backend can be used to switch globally from the original "R" implementation to the new "C++" back end. A new backend parameter has been added to ctx_tree(), vlmc() and tune_vlmc() to enable local back end selection.

The C++ implementation is significantly faster than the R implementation, at least by a factor 10. While it has been thoroughly tested, it is still considered experimental notably because it does not apply to COVLMC (setting the global option to "C++" has not effect on COVLMC model construction). For context trees and VLMC, results should not depend on the back end, at least within numerical precision. The only notable difference is the ordering of the contexts which differs between back ends: in a call to contexts(), the first context for the R back end will generally not be the first context for the C++ back end.

Other new features

  • contexts() can now report the positions of each context in the original time series
  • nodes of context trees can be extracted individually as ctx_node objects using the find_sequence() function. A collection of new functions can be used to manipulate the nodes and gain fine grain information on the corresponding sequences (issue #50).
  • by default, contexts() reports now contexts as a list of ctx_node objects
  • new functions predict.vlmc() and predict.covlmc() can be used to make one step ahead predictions of a time series based on a (CO)VLMC model (issue #46). Those function are documented in a new vignette (vignette("prediction"))
  • the log likelihood calculations performed by logLik.vlmc(), logLik.covlmc() loglikelihood() and loglikelihood.covlmc() have been revised, expanded to include three possible definitions of the likelihood function, and documented in a new vignette (vignette("likelihood"))
  • tune_vlmc() and tune_covlmc() can be used with the different likelihood function definitions
  • results of tune_vlmc() and tune_covlmc() can be plotted using base R graphics or ggplot2 (issue #36)
  • tune_covlmc() can trim the best model (and the initial one) if asked to
  • trim.covlmc() implements simple trimming for VGAM based objects (issue #48)
  • cutoff() uses a new tolerance parameter to avoid reporting cut off values that are almost identical due to numerical imprecision
  • simulate.vlmc() implements a user specified burn in period (issue #40)
  • simulate.vlmc() and simulate.covlmc() now handle the random generator state as does stats::simulate() (issue #56)

Minor improvements and bug fixes

  • Improved the test coverage (issue #54)
  • Fixed several bugs in internal sampling methods that made simulate.covlmc() unreliable for state spaces with three or more states
  • Fixed a bug in simulate.covlmc() that occurred in contexts with a longer self memory compared to their covariate memory
  • Fixed several bugs in metrics.vlmc() and align the results with the ones obtained by using direct calculation on the results of predict.vlmc()
  • Fixed several bugs related to degenerate VLMC (issue #55)
  • Fixed a bug in the likelihood calculation for internal context nodes
  • Improved type consistency by reporting counts as integers in contexts() results
  • Fixed documentation: all models can be adjusted on time series of logical values
  • Synchronized ctx_tree() documentation and its default value
  • Synchronized contexts() documentation and its default value
  • Added more trimming for COVLMC models in trim.covlmc()

mixvlmc 0.1.1

CRAN release: 2023-07-10

  • Added missing documentation about the return values of simulate.vlmc() and simulate.covlmc()

mixvlmc 0.1.0

  • Added a NEWS.md file to track changes to the package.
